<!-- pr-reviewer: cccde30bc7fdec3f6819981d1b7fcb33e1bbff7b -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a safety review because the change affects posted G-code.

Checks:
- The three posts stop the refused rapid. The feed, arc, and grblHAL cycle paths also stop when the first traverse is refused.
- X/Y stay unknown after the refusal. Later moves cannot use a refused position as a valid traverse.
- The tests cover the named refusal and the absence of X/Y motion. Tests with a stated clearance or retract plane still pass.
- The decision file explains why TinyG is included. No golden files changed. No UI files changed, so screenshots are not required.

Local results, after a clean trial merge with upstream/main at 703af8185f7cfc574050d0187502b4b42d6b67eb:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. All 17 post suites passed (144 tests). All 21 app suites passed (143 tests). No tests failed or were ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- Independent mutation 1: remove the grblHAL rapid refusal guard. The named no-plane test failed (8 passed, 1 failed).
- Independent mutation 2: remove the grblHAL cycle refusal guard. The first-move refusal test failed (8 passed, 1 failed).
- After both mutations, restore the original script and check that its bytes match. Run `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test first_traverse_clearance` again: all 9 tests passed. The worktree has no code changes.

Requested changes: none.

Notes: The full release gate and Windows tests were not run. No GitHub runner was used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
